page: Google Cloud Platform g1-small is a burstable, budget-oriented server instance belonging to the g1 family. It features 1 vCPU allocated from a shared physical Intel Xeon core running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding 1.7 GB of memory per core, and does not include any local storage or bundled GPUs. The processor features a 45 MB L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX, AES, and FMA, while lacking AVX-512 capabilities.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tiers of compute and memory capabilities. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests both yield a score of 1076.89, reflecting its shared-core architecture. Memory bandwidth is limited, with read-only large block speeds at 10.49 GB/sec and write speeds at 8.91 GB/sec. Passmark CPU and memory scores reside in the bottom 10% of tested hardware, with a database operations score of 564.91 and static web serving throughput of 0.54 GB/sec.

From a resource density and cost perspective, the g1-small is designed as a highly economical entry-level tier. The shared-core CPU allocation introduces performance tradeoffs under sustained workloads, making it unsuitable for intensive processing. It is best suited for lightweight, non-critical workloads such as basic web serving, small development environments, simple automation scripts, and low-traffic utility applications.
